chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: The two-string index bar
exercises.purpose: Train the one new physical skill F needs before adding the other fingers.

params.action: Lay the index finger flat across the B and high e strings at the 1st fret
params.cue: roll the finger slightly onto its side, toward the headstock

exercises.coaching: Before the whole chord, just this. Lay your index finger flat across the two thinnest strings at the first fret. Not the tip — the side. Roll it a little toward the headstock so the bony edge does the work, not the soft pad. Strum just those two strings. Both should ring. This one move is the only genuinely new thing in F.

exercises.name: Make F (four-string version)
exercises.purpose: Land a clean, honest F without the full barre.

params.fingers: index(1) bars B and high e at 1st, ring(3) G 2nd, pinky(4) D 3rd
params.muted: low E (6) and A (5) are NOT played
params.cue: strum only the top four strings

exercises.coaching: Keep that index bar. Now add ring finger on the G string, second fret, and pinky on the D string, third fret. Strum only the top four strings — skip the two fattest. That is a real F major. It has every note the chord needs. The full six-string barre F exists, but it is not required here and it stops more beginners than any other shape. This version is the one you will actually use.

exercises.name: C ↔ F, the change that matters
exercises.purpose: Make the F usable in real time, not just static.
exercises.coaching: C to F and back. Watch what your index finger does — in C it is on the B string first fret, and in F it stays on that same fret and just lies down flat. That is the whole trick. Do not lift and rebuild the hand; let the index pivot. Sixty beats a minute, one chord per four beats. Slow is the point.

exercises.name: Am – F – C – G
exercises.purpose: Put F straight into the most common loop in popular music.
exercises.coaching: Am, F, C, G. Round and round. This exact four-chord loop turns up in an enormous number of records, which means the moment this is smooth you are one strum pattern away from sounding like music instead of homework. If F is the chord that breaks the loop, slow the whole loop down until it does not.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: F is the chord that makes people quit. We are not going to do it the way that makes people quit. No full barre today — a four-string F that sounds right and that your hand can actually hold.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: One new skill first: the index finger lying flat across the two thin strings. Roll onto the side of the finger, not the pad.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Now add ring on G, pinky on D, and strum only the top four strings. That is F major, complete.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: C to F. Notice your index barely moves — it lies down rather than jumping. Let it pivot.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex4_intro: Am, F, C, G. The loop behind a startling number of songs. Get this smooth and a lot of doors open at once.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: You have F. Not a compromise F — a real one with every note in it, on four strings.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: F was the wall. It is behind you. Next we add A7, and after that the Mystery Songs open up.

lesson.title: New Chord: F (the four-string way)
lesson.one_line_promise: Get F without the barre that makes people quit.
objectives: Bar the index finger across two strings cleanly
Pivot C↔F without rebuilding the hand
Play Am-F-C-G as a continuous loop
unlocks: Mystery Songs requiring F: Californication, House of the Rising Sun, Stairway to Heaven
